subject: Throughput & SLA checklist for Dedicated capacity — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Cloud <avery@heatcap.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Throughput & SLA checklist for Dedicated capacity — follow-up and next steps

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discovery, I wanted to capture the pain, success criteria, and concrete asks so we have alignment before the tech deep-dive. Below is my read; please correct anything that’s off.

High-level pain & goals
- Current pain: unpredictable latency and steep per-token costs at peak; nightly batch jobs spike inference traffic and cause other services to degrade.
- Primary goal: stable 99th percentile latency under 300ms for live scoring; predictable per-request economics for budgeting.
- Secondary goal: strict data isolation and auditability for regulated data.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Frontend: Go microservices + k8s in GCP (us-central1)
- Model host: in-house Triton for some models, kuzsey-runner for others; mixing CPU and GPU inference
- Authentication/logging: Cloud Audit + internal logging pipeline

Key numbers I heard (please verify)
- Baseline steady-state: ~120 tps (short text, 64 tokens)
- Peak sustained windows: ~500 tps for ~45–60 minutes (daily)
- Burst events: up to ~1,200 tps for short spikes (5–15 minutes) during settlement windows
- Target latency: p99 <= 300ms; p95 <= 120ms

Operational constraints
- Must run in a dedicated GPU pool (no multi-tenant mixing for regulated models)
- Need autoscale to handle 2x baseline quickly, with predictable warm-up behavior
- Retention/audit: 13 months of request traces for compliance

Proposed next steps (from Redwood)
1) Tech deep-dive: 60–75m with your infra + model lead to validate request distribution and KV cache needs. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-11-11 10:00–11:15 PT or Thu 2026-11-12 08:00–09:15 PT.
2) We’ll send a preliminary throughput & SLA checklist and an architecture sketch (attached) so you can see the guardrails we recommend.
3) If the deep-dive looks good, propose a 4-week reserved pool POC: reserved baseline capacity to match 500 tps with burst buffer for 1,200 tps for 15m windows; measurable SLOs and cost report.

Action items I’d like from you
- Confirm/correct the numbers above (baseline/peak/burst).
- Add any other operational constraints we missed (data residency, regional isolation, E2E tracing).
- Confirm preferred deep-dive time or propose alternatives.

Attachments: throughput-sla-checklist.xlsx (checklist for us to fill together), redwood-dedicated-arch.png (example layout).

If this aligns, I’ll get Monica and Marcus to prepare the POC plan and tech agenda.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | (415) 555-0164
From: Avery Cloud <avery@heatcap.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Reed <samuel.reed@heatcap.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLA checklist for Dedicated capacity — follow-up and next steps

Karthik —

Thanks for the write-up, this is very close. A few quick corrections/clarifications:
- Baseline steady-state is ~140 tps (we had one daytime burst last week that pushed it up).
- Peak sustained windows are typically 450–550 tps, lasts around 30–50 minutes.
- Bursts: yes, up to ~1,200 tps but usually sub-10 minute for the big settlement windows; we’d like the burst to be covered without request throttling.
- Data residency: must keep EU customer data in europe region but our primary models for US customers are in us-central.

I’ve added our infra lead, Samuel, on the thread — he’ll be on the deep-dive and can share logs/metrics for the last two peak events.

Wed 11/11 10:00 PT works for us. Please send an invite.

—Avery
VP Product | HeatCap Finance
avery@heatcap.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Cloud <avery@heatcap.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Samuel Reed <samuel.reed@heatcap.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T12:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLA checklist for Dedicated capacity — follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the quick clarifications — updated notes below (I’ll also reflect this in the checklist).

Updated numbers (confirmed)
- Baseline: 140 tps (short text, ~64 tokens)
- Typical peak window: 450–550 tps for 30–50 minutes
- Burst events: up to 1,200 tps for ~5–10 minutes (must avoid throttling)
- Variant need: EU residency for EU customer requests — we’ll propose a regional pool for that traffic.

Prelim POC outline (high level)
- Duration: 4 weeks (min)
- Baseline reserved: capacity equivalent to 500 tps steady to account for headroom (2x baseline for safety during normal ops)
- Burst buffer: ability to support 1,200 tps for 10 minutes via warm standby + transient autoscale policy
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool per region (us-central, europe-west1) with separate logging buckets and KMS keys
- Success metrics: p99 <= 300ms for live scoring (measured at the API gateway), zero request throttling during verified settlement bursts, and per-token cost within quoted range

Prep for Wed 11/11 10:00 PT
- Samuel: please bring the performance logs (timestamps around the last two peak windows) and your current request-distribution histogram if available.
- Marcus & Monica: we’ll run through the checklist worksheet and show how we measure p99 and cost.

I’ll send calendar invite and attach an initial POC scope doc after this thread. Also attaching a SOC2 evidence request that some customers ask for earlier in the procurement flow — flagging now so we don’t get blocked later.

Next steps (short)
- I’ll send the invite + POC scope doc (by end of day).
- Samuel to share logs ahead of the deep-dive if possible.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to next week.

Karthik
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Avery Cloud <avery@heatcap.ai>, Samuel Reed <samuel.reed@heatcap.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLA checklist for Dedicated capacity — follow-up and next steps

Quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive:
- For the POC, we should confirm the largest model sequence length and KV-cache size so we can size GPU memory and plan quantization options. If their steady-state is 140 tps but model memory needs are high, baseline reserved compute could look different.
- Action: Karthik/Monica — can we include a 1-page table in the POC scope that asks for: model name/version, max sequence length, avg output tokens, KV cache bytes per request, and current quantization (fp16/int8)?

I’ll draft that table and attach to the POC scope doc.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
